effect: The lung exchange surface is connected to circulating blood, and the result shows why the air must be renewed.
reaction: The shrinking oxygen arrows make the need for breathing clearer.
reason: The pleural membranes link the lung side to the chest side, so they should prepare the lung route for chest movement.

reaction: The description makes the connection to chest movement clear.
reason: The breathing chest can attach to the chest-facing pleural sheet and renew the air in the lungs.
expectation: Chest movement will draw the lungs open and renew the air reaching the exchange surface.

effect: The breathing chest completed the oxygen-delivering circulation. The result connects chest expansion and air entry to oxygen transport through the blood and delivery to tissues.
reaction: The final route ties the pieces together clearly, though the pressure gauge adds a new detail that receives little explanation.

mostWorthwhile.text: Connecting the lung route to circulation was most worthwhile: the result showed why blood flow alone is insufficient if the air is not renewed.

leastWorthwhile.text: Adding the lining and then the capillary mesh felt predictable, although the separate steps made the two sides of the exchange surface clear.

surprise.text: The shrinking oxygen arrows showed that still air would gradually lose its ability to supply oxygen to flowing blood.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless. The pleural membranes were the least familiar connection, but the description of the wet sheets resisting separation helped explain their role.

continue.text: I would continue for another chapter: the final construction made me curious how the other body systems connect to this circulation.
